evaluations:
**Base UI** — An unstyled, accessible component library from the creators of Radix, Floating UI and Material UI ([README](https://github.com/mui/base-ui)). It is a solid, headless web layer. The README describes no agent-invocation model and no native story. It would need a separate action layer and native kits to meet this brief.

**Fluent UI** — Microsoft's design system, with React v9 (used by Microsoft 365), legacy v8, and Web Components ([README](https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui)). It is mature and accessible. This repo is web-only, and the README describes no agent-facing contract. The Web Components package is still versioned as beta in the README.

**OpenAI Apps SDK UI** — Tailwind 4 tokens plus Radix-based React components for ChatGPT apps ([README](https://github.com/openai/apps-sdk-ui)). It is good for the look and feel of UI inside ChatGPT. It is React-only and has no native kit. Its README documents no action or agent-tool model, so pair it with MCP Apps.

**MCP Apps** — An MCP extension where tools declare `ui://` HTML resources. The host renders them in a sandboxed iframe, and the UI can call tools back through the host ([README](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps)). It has broad host support (ChatGPT, Claude, VS Code, Goose). It is a delivery protocol, not a design system, and it is webview-based, so it is not native. It is the right transport layer, not the whole toolkit.

**AI Elements** — A shadcn-based set of chat components for AI SDK apps. Its own README warns that it will be deprecated at the end of November 2026 in favor of shadcn/ui's version ([README](https://github.com/vercel/ai-elements)). Do not start new work on it.

**MUI** — A comprehensive React implementation of Material Design, extended by MUI X ([README](https://github.com/mui/material-ui)). It is battle-tested for web UI. It is web-only and has no agent-facing contract in its README. It suits human dashboards, not cross-platform agent surfaces.

**Chakra UI** — An accessible React component system. It ships an MCP server package (`@chakra-ui/react-mcp`) so coding agents can read its docs ([README](https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui)). That helps agents that author UI. It does not help agents operate the UI, and it is web-only.

**Agent-native (Builder.io)** — An action-centric framework. `defineAction` with a zod schema becomes an agent tool, a UI call, and HTTP, MCP, A2A and CLI surfaces, with shared state and approvals ([README](https://github.com/BuilderIO/agent-native)). Its architecture is the closest to Ouro's one-action idea. It is not a component or design system, and it is TypeScript and web centered with no native kits.

**Flutter** — A single-codebase UI SDK for mobile, web and desktop, with Material and Cupertino widgets ([README](https://github.com/flutter/flutter)). It is strong for native reach, and A2UI has a Flutter renderer. It has no built-in agent-action or consent model, so you would add one. Its custom rendering is also less transparent than DOM semantics to browser-based agents.

**Tamagui** — Shares code across React and React Native through an optimizing compiler ([README](https://github.com/tamagui/tamagui)). It is good for web plus iOS and Android. Its README documents no agent features and no SwiftUI, Compose or Windows targets.

**Material 3 and Jetpack Compose** — Google's Android-native design system and toolkit, with theming, accessibility semantics and a large component set ([docs](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/designsystems/material3)). It is excellent for Android. It is Android-only and has no agent contract by itself. Ouro's Android kit shows Compose can host one.

**CopilotKit** — A full-stack agent UI stack over AG-UI, with chat, generative UI, shared state and human-in-the-loop. It supports A2UI and MCP Apps, and targets React, Angular, Vue and React Native, plus Slack and Teams ([README](https://github.com/CopilotKit/CopilotKit)). It is very capable for putting agents in front of users. It is not a design system, it has no SwiftUI or Compose kits, and it has commercial add-ons.

**Radix UI** — Low-level accessible React primitives for design systems ([README](https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives)). It is a good base layer, and other candidates (Apps SDK UI, shadcn) build on it. It is web-only and has no agent layer.

**Vercel UI SDK** — A beta library of framework-agnostic behaviors (focus, selection, popups, ARIA). It has React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and Web Component adapters and an agent skill, so agents author UI with it ([README](https://github.com/vercel-labs/ui)). It is an interesting design for agent authors. It is web-only and in beta under Vercel's beta terms, and it does not cover agent invocation of the UI.

**shadcn/ui** — Copy-in components you own, described as something to "build your own component library" ([README](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui)). Its registry format underlies AI Elements and Ouro HX. It is a flexible web foundation. It is web-only, and its README says nothing about agent actions or native platforms.

**SwiftUI and Apple Human Interface Guidelines** — Apple's declarative framework across iOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS and visionOS, with accessibility APIs ([docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui)). It is the authoritative native Apple path. It covers Apple only. A2UI and Ouro both target it as a renderer for cross-platform agent UI.

**json-render** — A Vercel Labs generative UI framework. You define a zod catalog, the AI emits a JSON spec, and renderers exist for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, React Native, PDF, email and others. It also has an MCP integration ([README](https://github.com/vercel-labs/json-render)). It is guardrailed and broad. Its native coverage is React Native only, and its README documents no consent or action-parity model.

**Ouro UI** — My pick. It has two halves: Ouro HX, shadcn-format React components, and Ouro AX, a CLI, API and MCP kit with an X-ray conformance checker. Agent-composed UI is validated as data against your catalog. Actions are declared once and generated into CLI, MCP, WebMCP, App Intent and button forms, with consent classes and typed refusals. It has native kits for SwiftUI, WinUI and Compose, and it accepts MCP Apps and A2UI payloads ([README](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui)). Risks: it is young, the Android kit is checked on emulators only, there is no Flutter or React Native path by design, and the benchmark and model-review evidence is self-published. An independent pilot would settle that.

**React Aria and React Spectrum** — Unstyled accessible components, React Stately state hooks, and Adobe's Spectrum implementation. It has strong internationalization and adaptive interaction ([README](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum)). It is the best web accessibility base here, and accessibility semantics also help agents. It has no agent-action layer, and it is web-first (Stately can be reused on other platforms).

**A2UI** — A protocol that expresses UI as validated data, streamed from agents to native renderers. Renderers exist for Lit, Angular, React and Flutter, and there are agent SDKs for Python and TypeScript ([README](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui)). It is the strongest open standard for cross-platform generative UI, with a clear trust boundary. It is not a human-facing design system, and it does not unify the actions a person presses with the tools an agent calls. That is Ouro's differentiator, and Ouro can consume A2UI.
